rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a Ni coating on W surfaces before Cu consolidation, whereas the paper used liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi alloy in molten Cu to selectively replace Ti-rich channels. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions sintering/infiltration and unspecified heat-transfer/irradiation conditions, while the paper used vacuum-sealed LMD at 1200 °C for 96 h and evaluated thermal conductivity up to 800 °C with 25 keV He+ irradiation. The regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes improved wetting and an interdiffusion barrier via a Ni layer, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on selective Ti dissolution, immiscibility-driven retention of W/Ta/V, and a spontaneously formed W-rich passivating interlayer. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved thermal conductivity relative to an untreated W–Cu composite, while the paper reports a specific increase from ~17 to ~75–140 W m−1 K−1 for a RHEA–Cu composite, surpassing pure W above 650 °C, and reduced He swelling. The hypothesis does not specify the property direction or magnitude in a way that matches the paper's result.
